question: Does an attention-weighted initialization of new-token embeddings beat a standard mean-of-context initialization on downstream classification of 20 Newsgroups text when about 200 domain tokens are added?
method: PPMI-SVD base embeddings (300d, top-5000 background vocab) + ~200 new downstream tokens initialised either by mean of window context vectors (baseline; logistic regression, C tuned by CV) or by PPMI-softmax-weighted context vectors (improved; attention init plus logistic-regression-or-RBF-SVM chosen and tuned by CV on train); document = mean token vector; macro-F1 on test.

dataset.name: 20 Newsgroups (4 categories: sci.space, rec.autos, comp.graphics, talk.politics.guns)

baseline: Mean-of-context initialization: each new token = unweighted mean of base vectors of words in its +/-5 co-occurrence window in downstream train text. Classifier: logistic regression with C tuned by 5-fold CV on train.
improved: Same contexts, but each context word weighted by a softmax over its PPMI score with the new token (attention-like weighting) before summing. Classifier: logistic regression or RBF-SVM, family and hyperparameters selected by 5-fold CV macro-F1 on train only.
notes: New-token vectors are frozen initialisations (no fine-tuning). The paper's exact token-distillation architecture is not given, so the attention is a PPMI-softmax proxy. Only the 4 categories are used and the base embeddings come from the other 16 categories. The improved model differs from the baseline in the initialisation and in the CV-tuned classifier search (LR vs RBF-SVM); the baseline classifier is unchanged. Mean +/- std over seeds 42-44 (SVD and CV folds); the train/test split is fixed. Test set is used only for final scoring.
